KOM-64.title: Build canonical tile-linked public waypoint system
KOM-64.description:
Effort: XL

Create a canonical KOME waypoint system tightly integrated with conquest tiles and visible to all players without relying on shared fellowships.

## Core rules

* A conquest tile may contain zero or one approved KOME waypoint.
* Every approved KOME waypoint must belong to exactly one conquest tile.
* Tiles without waypoints are valid and are expected to gain waypoints later through player development.
* KOME public waypoints are server-managed and globally synchronized. Players should not need to join a shared fellowship, manually add them, or manually remove them.
* Existing native LOTR waypoints and KOME-created public waypoints should coexist cleanly.
* Player-created waypoint proposals require admin approval before becoming globally visible or usable.
* Waypoint ownership is connected to tile ownership.
* Waypoint level is first-class KOME metadata and remains available for progression/travel/gameplay systems.

## Canonical waypoint state

An approved waypoint should at minimum have:

* stable waypoint ID
* tile ID
* display name
* world position
* source/type, such as native LOTR association or KOME public waypoint
* default owner
* current owner
* level
* approval metadata where relevant

Prefer deriving default/current ownership from the linked tile rather than maintaining independently mutable duplicate ownership state unless a later design explicitly requires waypoint and tile control to diverge.

## Public visibility

KOME-created approved waypoints should behave from the player's perspective like persistent world/default waypoints:

* visible to all applicable players
* synchronized automatically from server state
* persistent across logout/restart
* independent of fellowship membership
* removed/renamed/moved through KOME administration rather than requiring player cleanup

## Player proposal workflow

Any player may propose a waypoint while standing in a tile that has no approved waypoint.

A proposal does not create a real/public waypoint. It enters a pending state for admin review.

Admin approval must revalidate that the tile still has no approved waypoint before creating the canonical waypoint.

## Scope boundary

This parent issue establishes canonical waypoint data, public synchronization, tile relationship, proposal/approval workflow, ownership, and level metadata.

Normal waypoint fast-travel permission rules remain covered by <issue id="99b396e9-fbf0-49cf-9d27-459af40768e2" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-14/implement-waypoint-fast-travel-from-canonical-faction-relations">KOM-14</issue> and should consume this canonical waypoint state rather than being duplicated here.

Implementation is split into child issues so persistence, public synchronization, proposal approval, metadata, and migration can be validated independently.

KOM-65.title: Define canonical waypoint data model and one-waypoint-per-tile invariant
KOM-65.description:
Effort: M

Implement the canonical persisted waypoint record used by all KOME waypoint features.

## Requirements

* Each conquest tile may reference zero or one approved waypoint.
* Each approved waypoint must reference exactly one conquest tile.
* Enforce the one-waypoint-per-tile rule server-side, not only in UI.
* Preserve stable waypoint IDs across restarts.
* Store display name, world X/Y/Z position, tile ID, source/type, level, and approval metadata.
* Support both KOME-created public waypoints and associations to existing native LOTR waypoints where appropriate.
* Integrate with the canonical tile system from <issue id="61fbbc37-d792-49a8-b6d1-03a327bc0f7d" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-43/build-canonical-world-aware-conquest-tile-geometry-and-exact-map">KOM-43</issue> rather than maintaining independent geographic membership logic.
* Define deterministic validation for malformed or orphaned waypoint records.

## Acceptance

* A tile with no waypoint is valid.
* A second approved waypoint cannot be attached to the same tile.
* A waypoint cannot exist without a valid tile association unless explicitly represented as a native/non-KOME exception.
* Persistence survives restart without changing IDs or tile linkage.
* Other systems consume this one canonical waypoint record rather than duplicating state.

KOM-66.title: Implement globally synced KOME public waypoints independent of fellowships
KOM-66.description:
Effort: L

Add a server-managed public waypoint source so approved KOME waypoints are automatically visible to all applicable players without using a shared fellowship.

## Requirements

* Approved KOME public waypoints are synchronized from canonical server state.
* Players do not need to manually add or remove them.
* Joining/leaving fellowships must not affect KOME public waypoint visibility.
* KOME public waypoints must coexist with native LOTR/default waypoints.
* Renames, moves, removals, ownership metadata changes, and level changes should propagate cleanly.
* Persist across logout and server restart.
* Minimize client state and avoid duplicate waypoint entries after reconnect/reload.
* Prefer integration that behaves like persistent/default LOTR waypoints from the player's perspective without mutating unrelated native waypoint data unnecessarily.

## Acceptance

* A newly approved KOME waypoint appears for all connected players and for players joining later.
* Removing a waypoint removes it globally without requiring player cleanup.
* No shared fellowship is required.
* Reconnect/restart does not duplicate entries.
* Native LOTR waypoints continue to function normally.

KOM-67.title: Add player waypoint proposals with admin approval workflow
KOM-67.description:
Effort: L

Allow any player to propose a new public waypoint in a tile that currently has no approved waypoint, while requiring admin approval before it becomes canonical or globally visible.

## Player proposal

Provide a simple command/workflow equivalent to:

`/kome waypoint propose <name>`

Use the player's current world position and canonical tile resolution.

Validate before creating a proposal:

* player is inside a valid conquest tile
* tile has no approved waypoint
* submitted name is valid
* proposed position is valid
* handle existing pending proposals for the same tile explicitly rather than silently creating uncontrolled duplicates

Pending proposals must not behave as usable/public waypoints.

## Proposal state

Persist at minimum:

* proposal ID
* tile ID
* proposed name
* proposed world position
* submitting player
* submission time
* status: PENDING / APPROVED / REJECTED
* admin/review metadata and optional rejection reason

## Admin review

Provide workflows equivalent to:

* `/kome waypoint pending`
* `/kome waypoint inspect <proposal>`
* `/kome waypoint approve <proposal>`
* `/kome waypoint reject <proposal> [reason]`

Approval must revalidate canonical state, especially the one-waypoint-per-tile invariant, before creating the approved waypoint.

Allow an admin to adjust canonical values such as display name, exact position, or initial level during approval without forcing a player resubmission.

## Acceptance

* Any normal player can submit a valid proposal.
* Proposal is invisible as a public waypoint until approved.
* Admin approval creates exactly one canonical waypoint and triggers global synchronization.
* Admin rejection leaves no public waypoint behind.
* A stale proposal cannot create a second waypoint after another proposal was approved for that tile.
* Proposal history survives restart and remains auditable.

KOM-68.title: Connect waypoint ownership and level metadata to canonical tile state
KOM-68.description:
Effort: M

Make waypoint ownership and level first-class KOME metadata while preventing ownership state from drifting away from the linked tile.

## Ownership

* Every approved waypoint exposes default owner and current owner information.
* By default, derive waypoint default owner from the tile default owner.
* By default, derive waypoint current owner from the tile current owner.
* Tile ownership changes should automatically update what the waypoint reports without separate manual synchronization.
* Do not allow independent waypoint ownership divergence unless a future explicit gameplay design introduces settlement-level occupation.

## Level

* Store waypoint level independently from ownership.
* Level must persist across restart and ownership changes unless a later rule explicitly changes it.
* Expose level through the canonical waypoint API for future travel, settlement, progression, defense, or economy rules.
* Define safe validation/range handling without hardcoding gameplay meaning that has not yet been decided.

## Acceptance

* Capturing a tile changes the linked waypoint's reported current owner automatically.
* Historical/default ownership remains available.
* Waypoint level survives tile capture and restart.
* Fast-travel and UI systems can read ownership and level from one canonical source.

KOM-69.title: Migrate existing shared-fellowship waypoints into canonical public waypoints
KOM-69.description:
Effort: M

Replace the current operational dependence on a shared fellowship for KOME-managed waypoints.

## Requirements

* Inventory the waypoints currently being maintained through the shared fellowship and determine their corresponding conquest tiles.
* Preserve intended names and positions where valid.
* Convert eligible waypoints into canonical KOME public waypoints.
* Enforce the one-approved-waypoint-per-tile rule during migration.
* Flag duplicates, conflicting tile assignments, invalid positions, or waypoints outside canonical tiles for manual review.
* Do not require players to manually remove old fellowship waypoints as the long-term operating model.
* Provide a clean migration/cutover path that avoids duplicate visible waypoints during rollout.

## Acceptance

* Existing intended KOME waypoints are represented in canonical server state.
* Players no longer need the shared fellowship to receive KOME public waypoints.
* Duplicate or ambiguous legacy entries are reported instead of silently guessed.
* Cutover does not leave persistent duplicate public/fellowship waypoint entries for normal operation.

KOM-14.title: Implement waypoint fast travel from canonical faction relations
KOM-14.description:
Effort: L

Make KOME waypoint access consume the canonical faction relation state.

Required behavior:

* Wanderers/unpledged players retain normal LOTR travel access.
* Once pledged/serving a faction, waypoint access follows that faction's current canonical relation state.
* Enemy waypoints are not valid normal fast-travel destinations.
* Accepted relations grant the intended cross-faction waypoint access.
* Preserve native LOTR region unlock, cooldown, attack, sleeping, and global fast-travel configuration checks.
* Keep Join Battle deployment separate from normal fast travel.
* Support config-driven blocking of fast travel into active hostile/contested destinations if required by the battle implementation.
* Return clear denial reasons in UI.

AI implementation note: reuse KOMEWaypointAccessService and the transformer/request path where useful, but the canonical DiplomacyService must be the relationship authority. Retired waypoint/alliance-tier policy fields do not need compatibility support and can be removed once unused.

KOM-43.title: Build canonical world-aware conquest tile geometry and exact map borders
KOM-43.description:
## Current milestone: merged into dev (2026-09-22)

This update supersedes the historical candidate/checkpoint status below. Evidence comes from Dayne's local Codex reports and user acceptance in this conversation; tests were not independently rerun during this Linear update.

* Merged dev commit: [2559141cbc44a8e1f44811643381dd35673ccc59](<https://github.com/daynenewman/KOME-LOTR-Addon/commit/2559141cbc44a8e1f44811643381dd35673ccc59>).
* Validated integration: `96daae9e062c3337117dd3056aee72153be9bb3e`; merged tree reported identical. Local/remote dev synchronized and clean.
* Clean combined build: **951 passed, two existing Windows symlink skips**. All **6,055 gameplay expectations** passed. Disposable server completed two startup/save/stop cycles; 24 capitals READY.
* Dayne reported the combined client works well but could not fully test it. Detailed combined-client interaction, multiplayer and performance acceptance is not claimed.
* Shared server not deployed. Required schemas inherited from dev: root 4, Build 3, capital 1. No supported root-schema-3 migration.

Merged delivery includes canonical geometry/resolver (<issue id="30efefe2-2845-49fa-9c0e-c2bfd9142b12" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-55/define-canonical-conquest-tile-raster-and-exact-cell-boundary-policy">KOM-55</issue>/56), current-tile HUD (partial <issue id="c6b4eb78-eda5-4fa0-94c6-2754c827165f" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-60/add-player-and-physical-unit-tile-awareness-with-transition-events">KOM-60</issue>), reviewed land-gap and biome-boundary corrections (partial <issue id="c8b21e5b-74e1-46f4-96f8-5f698f76a5c9" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-59/audit-canonical-raster-coverage-and-classify-or-correct-unintended">KOM-59</issue>), explicit gameplay-default separation, and authoritative map rendering (<issue id="994f1c9f-5a08-43ed-8079-3a41d4ed4a46" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-61/rebuild-conquest-map-rendering-from-canonical-tile-geometry">KOM-61</issue>). Foundation and rendering implementation are complete.

Keep the parent open for remaining <issue id="a514e8d8-9cff-461f-ba39-53462e5ed069" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-57/validate-immutable-raster-snapshots-and-o1-tile-lookup-performance">KOM-57</issue> performance acceptance, <issue id="4b66c83f-d9c9-4745-b706-7dee533382af" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-58/model-explicit-uncapturable-geography-and-excluded-strategic-zones">KOM-58</issue> explicit geography metadata, <issue id="c8b21e5b-74e1-46f4-96f8-5f698f76a5c9" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-59/audit-canonical-raster-coverage-and-classify-or-correct-unintended">KOM-59</issue> unresolved geographic decisions, <issue id="c6b4eb78-eda5-4fa0-94c6-2754c827165f" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-60/add-player-and-physical-unit-tile-awareness-with-transition-events">KOM-60</issue> server/entity transitions, <issue id="a8fcc927-9f6c-4fb2-9396-d9f87630a0ba" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-62/add-optional-in-world-tile-border-visualization-and-admin-debug-tools">KOM-62</issue> optional in-world visualization, and <issue id="36b95b2c-1115-4d57-9f45-fd50b1d25417" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-63/run-tile-geometry-consistency-multiplayer-and-performance-acceptance">KOM-63</issue> broader acceptance. Map borders are not in-world border visualization. Public waypoint features remain separate and are not completed by capital integration.

---

Effort: XL

Create one canonical territory source shared by world lookup and conquest-map presentation. Preserve existing tile IDs, ownership, strategic adjacency, configuration, and persistence authorities. Membership depends on dimension and X/Z, independent of Y.

## Accepted architecture

The current authority is `reset_conquest_tile_ids.png`, its color-to-ID mapping, and LOTR's authoritative coordinate transform. This supersedes the earlier polygon/multipolygon implementation and chunk polygon-index requirements.

* Exact floor-based conversion, exactly one containing cell, no clamping or neighbor/nearest assignment.
* Irregular shapes, disconnected components, and empty areas are represented at raster-cell precision. No claim of subpixel precision.
* One common-side resolver serves server gameplay and client coordinate lookup; gameplay remains server-authoritative.
* Validated immutable decoded snapshots provide O(1) lookup, atomic publication, explicit invalidation/reload, and last-valid-snapshot preservation on failed replacement.
* No second tile registry, ownership cache, persisted derived raster, or automatic WorldData mutation.

## Gap policy and remaining geography work

An in-bounds gap means no assigned tile. It does not establish uncapturability, traversability, or a geographic reason. Capturability remains unknown without authoritative metadata.
Transparent and authoritatively excluded cells remain gaps. Unknown opaque colors and malformed mappings fail resource validation.
Cell (2291,58) remains a gap; (2292,58) resolves to T001. Do not auto-fill or repaint these as part of the foundation.
<issue id="4b66c83f-d9c9-4745-b706-7dee533382af" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-58/model-explicit-uncapturable-geography-and-excluded-strategic-zones">KOM-58</issue> defines explicit geographic classification. <issue id="c8b21e5b-74e1-46f4-96f8-5f698f76a5c9" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-59/migrate-existing-conquest-map-tiles-into-canonical-world-geometry">KOM-59</issue> audits gaps and proposes reviewed resource corrections. The broader goal remains no unexplained accidental strips between normal tiles. Reassignment requires an explicit data decision, never runtime inference.
Outside-mask is a technical extent result, not complete classification of every non-playable area.

## Child stages

* <issue id="30efefe2-2845-49fa-9c0e-c2bfd9142b12" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-55/define-canonical-conquest-tile-geometry-and-shared-boundary-data-model">KOM-55</issue>: canonical raster representation and boundary policy.
* <issue id="bc171cb5-3d66-4263-8b0d-d10621a1a97d" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-56/implement-server-authoritative-world-xz-to-conquest-tile-resolver">KOM-56</issue>: shared dimension-aware resolver and existing caller reconciliation.
* <issue id="a514e8d8-9cff-461f-ba39-53462e5ed069" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-57/add-chunk-level-spatial-index-and-cache-for-tile-resolution">KOM-57</issue>: immutable snapshot performance/lifecycle validation.
* <issue id="4b66c83f-d9c9-4745-b706-7dee533382af" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-58/model-explicit-uncapturable-geography-and-excluded-strategic-zones">KOM-58</issue>: explicit uncapturable geography.
* <issue id="c8b21e5b-74e1-46f4-96f8-5f698f76a5c9" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-59/migrate-existing-conquest-map-tiles-into-canonical-world-geometry">KOM-59</issue>: coverage audit and reviewed resource corrections.
* <issue id="c6b4eb78-eda5-4fa0-94c6-2754c827165f" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-60/add-player-and-physical-unit-tile-awareness-with-transition-events">KOM-60</issue>: player/unit awareness and transition events.
* <issue id="994f1c9f-5a08-43ed-8079-3a41d4ed4a46" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-61/rebuild-conquest-map-rendering-from-canonical-tile-geometry">KOM-61</issue>: map fills and display borders derived from canonical cells.
* <issue id="a8fcc927-9f6c-4fb2-9396-d9f87630a0ba" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-62/add-optional-in-world-tile-border-visualization-and-admin-debug-tools">KOM-62</issue>: optional nearby in-world borders and further diagnostics.
* <issue id="36b95b2c-1115-4d57-9f45-fd50b1d25417" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-63/run-tile-geometry-consistency-multiplayer-and-performance-acceptance">KOM-63</issue>: staged foundation and full-system acceptance.

World positions, map lookup, and final rendered fills must agree. Visual border width cannot change membership. Lookup reconciliation alone does not complete rendering, player indicators, or entity tracking.
Measure multiple-player and lower-spec performance. Do not add a redundant index without demonstrated need.

## Scope and completion

War, movement, population, and capture-rule redesign remain outside this issue. A standalone tile editor is deferred by Dayne.
Foundation testing may proceed before later stages. Keep the parent open until broader acceptance is met. Its existing dependency blocking <issue id="62cf7288-5bc1-4e43-8fa4-b895cee2c547" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-65/define-canonical-waypoint-data-model-and-one-waypoint-per-tile">KOM-65</issue> remains; this does not block testing <issue id="61fbbc37-d792-49a8-b6d1-03a327bc0f7d" href="https://linear.app/kome-development/issue/KOM-43/build-canonical-world-aware-conquest-tile-geometry-and-exact-map">KOM-43</issue> itself.

## Reported checkpoint: 2026-09-19

Source: Dayne's local Codex report, not independently rerun from Linear.

* Branch: `dayne/tile-world-resolution-dev`; base/HEAD: `d6bb856f2a06d39f15458b042bb48071286655de`.
* 24 changed paths: 14 modified, 10 untracked; empty index; no candidate commit/push/merge.
* Focused tests: 171 passed. Clean test/build: 741 discovered, 739 passed, two existing platform-dependent skips, zero failures/errors. Production packaging passed.
* Original worktree, recovery package, and protected stash preserved.
* Dedicated-server startup, matching-client connection, map/boundary interaction, Build and permission checks remain pending.
* Implementation is ready for review and live validation, not completed or deployed.
